ORTIA SMUGGLERS' PARADISE

By: Ntokozo Miya | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Anti-drug trafficking groups say corruption has turned OR Tambo International Airport into a smugglers' paradise but authorities disagree, and have busts to back it up.

Unique Selling Point:
We speak to people on different ends of the international drug trade – a woman who smuggled drugs through OR Tambo and did time in a Hong Kong prison for trafficking, a chaplain in a Hong Kong prison who counsels South Africans imprisoned abroad and an organization whose research shows that drug syndicates find it easier to travel through OR Tambo airport with drugs.

Summary:
A recent report by Locked Up Abroad SA states that most drug traffickers imprisoned in other countries flew from the OR Tambo International Airport. We explore why this is the case, bearing in mind that most international flights depart from OR Tambo. We interrogate the stats and pose hard questions to authorities about alleged corruption and collusion with drug syndicates.

Further information:
According to a report by organisations Baagi Ba and Locked Up in A Foreign Country, airports around the world are seeing an unprecedented rise in drug trafficking cases via OR Tambo Airport. Hong Kong prison chaplain John Wotherspoon alleged that nearly 20% of all people arrested in Hong Kong airport in 2018 and 2019 for the possession of illegal substances brought drugs from Johannesburg via OR Tambo. Of the 46 South Africans locked up in Hong Kong, 44 are for drug-related offences, and all of the 31 South Africans locked up in mainland China prisons are in jail for drug-related offences. According to SA’s department of international relations and co-operation, 790 South Africans were incarcerated abroad as of November 30 last year.

Press Release:


A Smuggler’s Paradise
Luggage runs through the X-ray scanners, a passenger undergoes an intrusive body search and sniffer dogs roam the halls – but despite all these security measures, O.R .Tambo International has gained a reputation for being a drug smuggler’s paradise. Carte Blanche investigates why this airport has seemingly become an easy exit point for international mules.
Producer: Ntokozo Miya and Mduduzi Miya | Presenter: Macfarlane Moleli


Script:


OR TAMBO – FOR MIX

INTRO - The OR Tambo airport in Johannesburg, where the majority of international flights from South Africa depart, processes over twenty million passengers each year. Alert customs agents, security guards and police officers patrol the facility. And even with the security and checkpoint upgrades implemented over the years, the airport also relies on “man's best friend” to sniff out guns and drugs. Despite all this, some say the airport remains top choice for syndicates distributing narcotics across the globe.
PATRICIA GERBER – LOCKED UP ABROAD

The syndicates are in cahoots with the airport authorities as well as some of the corrupt SAPS, and so why would they want to use another airport?
NOKWAZI MEMELA – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER

You can have sniffer dogs and whatever else but if there are people taking bribes to let you through, even the dogs are useless.
LEHLOHONOLO LETSOALO – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER

It's a lot of people involved.
VO – According to the Department of International Relations, there are seven hundred and ninety South Africans doing time abroad – seventy-one per cent of them for drug-related crimes. But prisoner rights advocates believe the figure is higher because some arrests and convictions are not reported to the relevant authorities.

Many of the prisoners managed to smuggle banned substances through the OR Tambo airport before being nabbed in other countries. Some arrests even made international headlines...
ARIRANG NEWS ANCHOR

A South African woman was caught at Kime airport while trying to smuggle marijuana into South Korea.
NST KENYA NEWS ANCHOR

Anti-narcotics unit detectives are holding two South African nationals in an ongoing swoop on drug traffickers.
ARIRANG NEWS ANCHOR

This is the largest amount of drugs caught coming into Kime airport from South Africa in the last ten years.
VO – Patricia Gerber established the Locked Up Abroad organisation after her own son was arrested for drug trafficking inMauritius in 2007. Through her work, she interacts with prisoners and authorities in other countries. She says narcotics distributors prefer to travel from OR Tambo.
PATRICIA GERBER – LOCKED UP ABROAD - CLIP NO: 773_7333_01

06:20 – They are paying money to the corrupt police and airport officials. 01:21 – The drugs are taken though OR Tambo, not one of them are stopped.

LINK - 00:00:35:06 – Airports are full of people excited at the prospect of a holiday abroad, visiting family in another country or doing business on a global scale. And then there are those nervously traveling with narcotics that could land them in prison for life.
VO – Lehlohonolo Letsoalo from Atteridgeville near Pretoria was one such traveler about a decade ago.

He was a courier for a drug syndicate with overseas networks and was paid extra to recruit people to smuggle marijuana and cocaine on international flights from OR Tambo.
LEHLOHONOLO LETSOALO – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER

It was easy. Some were promised jobs, that they'll get jobs in the UK. Some knew, some didn't know.
VO – Each successful trip netted him thousands of rands.
LEHLOHONOLO LETSOALO – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER

When you convert it, it's about almost a R100k, South African currency.
VO – He says safe passage through OR Tambo was pre-arranged by his bosses. But he did carry cash in case he had to bribe officials in other countries.
LEHLOHONOLO LETSOALO – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER

One of the guys in the police who were working in Zambia asked me for momeny, I think I gave him about ten thousand South African rands.
VO – When international authorities became critical of flights arriving from OR Tambo as the route proved to be a favorite among traffickers, Lehlohonolo stopped flying directly from the airport. But even that tactic did not keep him out of jail.
MAC QUESTION – how long were you doing this, how many trips had you done?

LEHLOHONOLO LETSOALO – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER

I did about nine trips, all in all. I was caught on my tenth trip. I was caught coming from Zambia. From Johannesburg going to Zambia, from Zambia to the UK.
VO – He was arrested at London's Heathrow Airport. Lehlohonolo went on to serve a little over one year of a five year sentence before he was given amnesty and deported back to SA.
LINK - 00:00:10:00 – Going through an airport with a few grams of a banned substance is a one-man job but it seems smuggling quantities as much as ten kilograms or more requires a well-coordinated team effort.
VO – Lehlohonolo says as long as police are not paid a decent salary, they will always be open to corruption.
LEHLOHONOLO LETSOALO – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER

You find someone who's given a big task to catch someone with ten million and you give him R5000 per month. He can't even afford basic needs and you go there with R100 000, he's never even seen R100 000 in his life.
VO – In 2007, Alexandra township's Nokwazi Memela started going to a church in Yeoville. The pastor was moved by her circumstances and said he wanted to help.


NOKWAZI MEMELA – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER

He remarked that I live in an RDP house with five children and I'm a domestic worker.
VO – She was introduced to a senior pastor who told her there was a job for her in Iran
NOKWAZI MEMELA – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER

There was a man in Iran who had a company that exports carpets from Iran to China and he needed women to do that work. They said I should take the job so I could buy a bigger house and take my children to better schools.
VO – And just like that, Nokwazi was off to Iran – her first trip overseas.
NOKWAZI MEMELA – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER

The church provided everything including the passport and visa, and even bought the ticket. hey gave me luggage and I was taken to OR Tambo. I took a flight from OR Tambo and landed in Dubai. From there, I flew to Iran. When I got to Iran, I went to the hotel.
VO – Nokwazi never checked what was inside the big suitcase but says the man who met her in Iran was very happy to receive it. The man introduced her to other women at the Iranian hotel.
NOKWAZI MEMELA – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER

That's when they told us that there was no job exporting carpets and that we had to swallow drugs and take them from Iran to China. In Iran, they searched us and found the drugs. We were arrested, When I heard them say “heroin”, I thought it was someone's name.
VO – She'd been forced to swallow the drugs but she didn't know exactly what they were.
NOKWAZI MEMELA – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER

I was taken to theatre for an operation to remove the drugs. I woke up the next day in a ward. I looked at my stomach. There was a hole and exposed white flesh. I asked if they would close the open wound and they said I should not worry about it because I would be executed anyway.
VO – She did eventually get stitches a week later. Nokwazi was sentenced to die, but she was lucky. For reasons still unclear to her, after 7 years in prison awaiting a death sentence, she was released in 2014. Back home, she tried to confront the men who sent her on the doomed mission.
NOKWAZI MEMELA – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER

They told me they would send me money. “We know that you need money.” They deposited R150.
VO – She never saw or heard from the pastors again.

Patricia says cartels often recruit poor and naive people.
PATRICIA GERBER – LOCKED UP ABROAD

They've never been out of this country. They've never bought their own air tickets. Everything is done for them here. The drugs are taken though OR Tambo, not one of them are stopped. NO MUSIC – WILL CUT OUT
LINK - Authorities dispute perceptions that OR Tambo is a narcotics highway and say their anti-drug trafficking efforts have seen many smuggling operations crash and burn.


VO – SARS customs officials are tasked with ensuring that goods that enter South African borders are legal and where necessary, taxed accordingly, while ACSA, Airports Company South Africa, provides systems and infrastructure for points of entry. SARS and ACSA declined to comment on assertions that OR Tambo is a key gateway to the international drug trade.

They directed us to SAPS spokesperson Brigadier Vishnu Naidoo because it is the responsibility of the police to confiscate drugs discovered at the airport and arrest perpetrators.
BRIG. VISHNU NAIDU – SAPS

For people to say...that it's easy for people to take drugs through South Africa, primarily through OR Tambo international airport is misleading. For the 2018 financial year, we arrested 98 drug mules, that is almost two per week.
VO – In the beginning of February, police had their hands full after three people tried to smuggle cocaine worth over thirty million rands into the country in one day. A man and a woman arrived on South American flights while a third man was on his way to Hong Kong.
BRIG. VISH NAIDU – SAPS

That is an indication that we do have the capacity and capabilities to be able to deal with this part of smuggling.
VO – With over seventy thousand people going through the airport daily, some drug traffickers do slip through the cracks.
MAC – Corruption does also play a huge role, right?

BRIG – There's absolutely no denying that Macfarlane because we have arrested our own. We have arrested members of other departments at OR Tambo international airport. We implemented a new, revised intervention strategy from 2017. Part of that intervention strategy entailed vetting, screening and lifestyle audits of all employees.
VO – Nokwazi now dedicates herself to visiting churches to warn people about the recruitment methods of syndicates.

Lehlohonolo runs the Aga Sechaba centre for people addicted to drugs as well as those who want out of a life of crime. This is one way he makes up for all the lives that were destroyed by the drugs he sold.

PROMO

Authorities dispute perceptions that the OR Tambo airport is a narcotics highway, and say their anti-drug trafficking efforts have seen many smuggling operations crash and burn.

Convicted drug traffickers say corruption and lax security have turned OR Tambo airport into a smugglers' paradise but authorities disagree, and have busts to back it up.

More South Africans are arrested abroad for drugs smuggled through OR Tambo international airport, we investigate whether this facility has become a smugglers' paradise.

LINK - 00:00:10:00 – Going through an airport with a few grams of a banned substance is a one-man job but it seems smuggling quantities as much as ten kilograms or more requires a well-coordinated team effort. VO – Lehlohonolo says as long as police are not paid a decent salary, they will always be open to corruption. LEHLOHONOLO LETSOALO – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER You find someone who's given a big task to catch someone with ten million and you give him R5000 per month. He can't even afford basic needs and you go there with R100 000, he's never even seen R100 000 in his life. VO – In 2007, Alexandra township's Nokwazi Memela started going to a church in Yeoville. The pastor was moved by her circumstances and said he wanted to help. NOKWAZI MEMELA – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER He remarked that I live in an RDP house with five children and I'm a domestic worker. VO – She was introduced to a senior pastor who told her there was a job for her in Iran NOKWAZI MEMELA – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER There was a man in Iran who had a company that exports carpets from Iran to China and he needed women to do that work. They said I should take the job so I could buy a bigger house and take my children to better schools. VO – And just like that, Nokwazi was off to Iran – her first trip overseas. NOKWAZI MEMELA – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER The church provided everything including the passport and visa, and even bought the ticket. hey gave me luggage and I was taken to OR Tambo. I took a flight from OR Tambo and landed in Dubai. From there, I flew to Iran. When I got to Iran, I went to the hotel. VO – Nokwazi never checked what was inside the big suitcase but says the man who met her in Iran was very happy to receive it. The man introduced her to other women at the Iranian hotel. NOKWAZI MEMELA – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER That's when they told us that there was no job exporting carpets and that we had to swallow drugs and take them from Iran to China. In Iran, they searched us and found the drugs. We were arrested, When I heard them say “heroin”, I thought it was someone's name. VO – She'd been forced to swallow the drugs but she didn't know exactly what they were. NOKWAZI MEMELA – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER I was taken to theatre for an operation to remove the drugs. I woke up the next day in a ward. I looked at my stomach. There was a hole and exposed white flesh. I asked if they would close the open wound and they said I should not worry about it because I would be executed anyway. VO – She did eventually get stitches a week later. Nokwazi was sentenced to die, but she was lucky. For reasons still unclear to her, after 7 years in prison awaiting a death sentence, she was released in 2014. Back home, she tried to confront the men who sent her on the doomed mission. NOKWAZI MEMELA – CONVICTED DRUG TRAFFICKER They told me they would send me money. “We know that you need money.” They deposited R150. VO – She never saw or heard from the pastors again. Patricia says cartels often recruit poor and naive people. PATRICIA GERBER – LOCKED UP ABROAD They've never been out of this country. They've never bought their own air tickets. Everything is done for them here. The drugs are taken though OR Tambo, not one of them are stopped. NO MUSIC – WILL CUT OUT LINK - Authorities dispute perceptions that OR Tambo is a narcotics highway and say their anti-drug trafficking efforts have seen many smuggling operations crash and burn. VO – SARS customs officials are tasked with ensuring that goods that enter South African borders are legal and where necessary, taxed accordingly, while ACSA, Airports Company South Africa, provides systems and infrastructure for points of entry. SARS and ACSA declined to comment on assertions that OR Tambo is a key gateway to the international drug trade. They directed us to SAPS spokesperson Brigadier Vishnu Naidoo because it is the responsibility of the police to confiscate drugs discovered at the airport and arrest perpetrators. BRIG. VISHNU NAIDU – SAPS For people to say...that it's easy for people to take drugs through South Africa, primarily through OR Tambo international airport is misleading. For the 2018 financial year, we arrested 98 drug mules, that is almost two per week. VO – In the beginning of February, police had their hands full after three people tried to smuggle cocaine worth over thirty million rands into the country in one day. A man and a woman arrived on South American flights while a third man was on his way to Hong Kong. BRIG. VISH NAIDU – SAPS That is an indication that we do have the capacity and capabilities to be able to deal with this part of smuggling. VO – With over seventy thousand people going through the airport daily, some drug traffickers do slip through the cracks. MAC – Corruption does also play a huge role, right? BRIG – There's absolutely no denying that Macfarlane because we have arrested our own. We have arrested members of other departments at OR Tambo international airport. We implemented a new, revised intervention strategy from 2017. Part of that intervention strategy entailed vetting, screening and lifestyle audits of all employees. VO – Nokwazi now dedicates herself to visiting churches to warn people about the recruitment methods of syndicates. Lehlohonolo runs the Aga Sechaba centre for people addicted to drugs as well as those who want out of a life of crime. This is one way he makes up for all the lives that were destroyed by the drugs he sold. PROMO Authorities dispute perceptions that the OR Tambo airport is a narcotics highway, and say their anti-drug trafficking efforts have seen many smuggling operations crash and burn. Convicted drug traffickers say corruption and lax security have turned OR Tambo airport into a smugglers' paradise but authorities disagree, and have busts to back it up. More South Africans are arrested abroad for drugs smuggled through OR Tambo international airport, we investigate whether this facility has become a smugglers' paradise.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Anti-drug trafficking groups say corruption has turned OR Tambo International Airport into a smugglers' paradise but authorities disagree, and have busts to back it up.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We speak to people on different ends of the international drug trade – a woman who smuggled drugs through OR Tambo and did time in a Hong Kong prison for trafficking, a chaplain in a Hong Kong prison who counsels South Africans imprisoned abroad and an organization whose research shows that drug syndicates find it easier to travel through OR Tambo airport with drugs.
metadata.Summary: A recent report by Locked Up Abroad SA states that most drug traffickers imprisoned in other countries flew from the OR Tambo International Airport. We explore why this is the case, bearing in mind that most international flights depart from OR Tambo. We interrogate the stats and pose hard questions to authorities about alleged corruption and collusion with drug syndicates.
metadata.Further information: According to a report by organisations Baagi Ba and Locked Up in A Foreign Country, airports around the world are seeing an unprecedented rise in drug trafficking cases via OR Tambo Airport. Hong Kong prison chaplain John Wotherspoon alleged that nearly 20% of all people arrested in Hong Kong airport in 2018 and 2019 for the possession of illegal substances brought drugs from Johannesburg via OR Tambo. Of the 46 South Africans locked up in Hong Kong, 44 are for drug-related offences, and all of the 31 South Africans locked up in mainland China prisons are in jail for drug-related offences. According to SA’s department of international relations and co-operation, 790 South Africans were incarcerated abroad as of November 30 last year.
